problem: The line $y=2x$ intersects the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x-2},$ for $k\ne 0,$ only once. What is the value of $k?$

examples.problem: The line $y=2x+3$ does not intersect the reciprocal function $y=\dfrac{k}{x+3}$, where $k \neq 0$. What is the range of possible values of $k?$
examples.worked_solution:
To determine whether the line $y=2x+3$ intersects the reciprocal function $y=\dfrac{k}{x+3},$ we need to solve the following system of equations for the two curves:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=\frac{k}{x+3} \\ y=2x+3\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and simplifying, we get a quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k}{x+3} & =2x+3 \\ k & =(2x+3)(x+3) \\ k & =2{x}^{2}+9x+9 \\ 2{x}^{2}+9x+9-k & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the quadratic formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-9\pm \sqrt{{9}^{2}-4(2)(9-k)}}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{-9\pm \sqrt{81-72+8k}}{4} \\  & =\frac{-9\pm \sqrt{9+8k}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

For the line *not* to intersect the reciprocal function, the quadratic formula above must *not* give any real solutions.

So, the expression inside the square root must be negative:

$$
\begin{aligned}9+8k & <0 \\ 8k & <-9 \\ k & <-\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of possible values of $k$ is $k<-\dfrac{9}{8}.$

feedback.problem: If the line $y=-2x-1$ and the curve $y=\frac{3}{x+3}+1$ intersect at the point $(p,q),$ then $p+q=$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=-2x-1 &  \\ y=\frac{3}{x+3}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get a quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-1 & =\frac{3}{x+3}+1 \\ -2x-2 & =\frac{3}{x+3} \\ (-2x-2)(x+3) & =3 \\ -2{x}^{2}-8x-6 & =3 \\ 2{x}^{2}+8x+9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the quadratic formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{{8}^{2}-4(2)(9)}}{2(2)} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{64-72}}{4} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{-8}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root of a negative number is not a real number, so there are no real solutions. Consequently, the line $y=-2x-1$ does not intersect the hyperbola $y=\frac{3}{x+3}+1.$
